analysis:
Examined: (1) new AdmissionRateEstimators.swift (DeadlineAdmissionFixes, MeasuredDecodeStep, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate); (2) WholeMacServiceBudget.swift new isIdle(except:) helper; (3) LaunchAgent.swift adding DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES to the launchd passthrough env list.

Security-relevant observations: the changes affect only local first-token deadline admission arithmetic (availability/performance), not the coordinator-provider crypto, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), prefix cache (T-041) or key custody. No plaintext, key, or authorization material is touched. The env toggle is read from the provider process environment and the launchd plist passthrough only carries a rollback flag; the local operator is already in the adversary set (ADV-001) and a local operator can already disable admission modes via PrefillDeadlineMode, so no new privilege boundary is crossed. The toggle parsing is fail-open to enabled (default true) and non-numeric values map to enabled, which is benign.

IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve guards non-finite and non-positive inputs. MeasuredDecodeStep.observe guards tps finite and positive; tokensPerSecond divides by seconds with a guard on seconds > 0 (a division by zero yields inf or NaN but is filtered by isFinite). The anchor floor bounds how low the estimate can be driven, which limits a contended/malicious sample from forcing over-refusal. A provider (ADV-001) can still influence its own admission rate, which only affects its own availability and is not a consumer-impacting security issue.

isIdle(except:) holds the lock and is read-only, with no reentrancy risk. Its callers are not in the supplied evidence; whether they use it to gate calibration evidence safely (e.g. with the evidenceGuard invalidation semantics) is an unverified integration question, though the helper itself introduces no regression. CBv2DecodeRateShape.isValid and EnginePerformanceMeasurements.freshness are outside the supplied evidence.

No findings.
